messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: page fired for SERVICE: inference-az4 (region az4) at 1777771234. Symptom: increased 5xx rate and health check failures on nodes serving model shard set-az4. Severity: P1. Pager runbook ID: RB-serve-02.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert: incident INC-2026-0932 created and assigned to "Alice (oncall)". Escalation policy: primary -> seq-1.

Alice (oncall): Acked. I'm seeing spike in 5xx from LB logs, consistent with K8s readiness probe failures. Spawning a thread here to coordinate. 

Ben (eng-sre): On it — looking at autoscaler and GPU node pool. Early hypothesis: kernel OOMs or NVMe IO bottle-neck causing kubelet evictions. Pulling node metrics.

Carla (sre-lead): @Alice @Ben if autoscaler not responding, prepare manual scale and consider routing fallback to us-west. Check prefix cache retention too. Notify product /support for customer impact.

Alice (oncall): Quick checks: 
```
# recent kube evictions
kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector type=Warning | tail -n 20
# pod restarts
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep az4
```
Results: 12 pods in CrashLoopBackOff across az4 shard replicaset. Node pressure shows memory high.

David (platform): I can spin up replacement nodes in az4 now but want to avoid further evictions if underlying disk issue. Provisioning additional nodes in us-west as warm-failover. Starting `redwoodctl infra scale --pool=us-west-warm --count=4`.

Maria (support): Heads-up: we've already seen 3 customer reports for inference timeouts in EU customers routed to az4. Filing interim notice to customers: "We're investigating degraded inference in region az4; traffic may be routed to another region. No data loss reported."

Ben (eng-sre): Checking kubelet logs on affected node: 
```
Mar 02 09:11:42 node-az4-12 kubelet[...]: eviction manager: attempting signal no memory left: reclaim failed
Mar 02 09:11:43 node-az4-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (python) score 987
```
This looks like OOMs across multiple nodes. Could be memory leak in a recent model rollout. Rolling back latest model variant on az4 may help.

Alice (oncall): Do we have canary rollback options? Last deploy timestamp 1777769000 for model-v2-quant. I will trigger an automated rollback to model-v1 on az4 only. Command: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --env=prod --region=az4 --model=model-v1 --force`.

Carla (sre-lead): Good. While rollback proceeds, prepare routing fallback policy: set `route-policy=divert` for az4 -> us-west until healthy. Ben, can you verify compatibility of cache keys across regions?

Ben (eng-sre): Cache is prefix-keyed; cross-region is safe, but warm-up will cause cold-starts and increased latency temporarily. Setting gradual divert: 0% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 mins. Command I've queued: 
```
redwoodctl routing set-divert --from=az4 --to=us-west --steps=3 --step-interval=120s
```

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Alice acknowledged, escalation paused. Next escalation window in 8 minutes if no resolution.

incident-bot: Runbook step RB-serve-02: 
1) Acknowledge and annotate incident.
2) Check node health and evictions.
3) If OOM across nodes -> rollback model variant on affected shard.
4) If rollback insufficient -> activate regional fallback and scale warm pool.
5) Communicate impact to support and customers.
```
# runbook note: execute rollback only for az4 to avoid global regressions
```

Alice (oncall): Triggered rollback at 1777771298. Monitoring pod status.

Ben (eng-sre): Rollback applied. I'm seeing pods restart and memory pressure easing on nodes: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference | grep az4
inference-az4-1   Running   0    2m
inference-az4-2   Running   0    1m
```

Maria (support): Updating support status page: "Mitigation in progress: model rollback in az4 and traffic divert preparing. Some customers may see increased latency as traffic rebalances." (noted: ticket IDs #4523, #4526).

David (platform): Starting routing divert now (gradual). Command executed: `redwoodctl routing set-divert --from=az4 --to=us-west --steps=3`. Pushing announcement to edge config.

Carla (sre-lead): Good. Keep watch on error rate and per-route latency. If 5xx drops below 0.5% for 10m, we can begin reintroducing traffic to az4. If not, we'll keep divert active and scale more capacity in us-west.

Ben (eng-sre): Observability: 5xx rate on az4 was 7.2% at peak, now down to 1.1% after rollback and divert step-1. Pod OOMs stopped.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: escalation suppressed by Alice. Reminder: mark incident with postmortem owner when resolved.

Alice (oncall): Confirming failover activation: divert at 100% now. Customers routed away from az4. Will keep monitoring for 30m, then start controlled re-enable after smoke tests.

Maria (support): Sent interim customer notification and updated status page. Received confirmation from one large customer that their traffic is restored via us-west.

Carla (sre-lead): Next steps: 1) full node pool health sweep in az4; 2) identify root cause of OOMs (possible model memory regression) with ML team; 3) postmortem owner: Ben. Please collect heap dumps and model runtime traces.

Ben (eng-sre): Will take postmortem. Captured heap profiles and model allocation traces. Saved to internal S3: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0932/profiles/.

Alice (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated at 1777771450. Keeping thread open for postmortem notes and customer callback. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0932 status: mitigated (traffic diverted, rollback applied). Please file postmortem within 72 hours."
